title: Embed synthetic-led traffic shepherding and tenant degradation contracts into runtime PRD
creator: Priya Narang
description:
Summary: Translate recent multi-tenant latency incident postmortem into concrete PRD requirements that add a synthetic-driven traffic shepherding layer and per-tenant degradation contracts. Goal: reduce blast radius for tail-latency events by enabling automated, observable, and reversible degraded-mode mitigations that can be enacted via the control plane or automatically when SLO gates trip. This PRD update captures scope, APIs, UX, telemetry, runbooks, and acceptance checks required for engineering to implement a production-grade feature set compatible with Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
Problem context: In the incident, recoveries relied on manual operator decisions and ad-hoc routing changes. Tenants with bursty embeddings workloads experienced disproportionate tail latency and cache churn. Postmortem action items recommended: (1) tenant-level degradation budgets, (2) automated canary traffic shepherding to warm standby pools, and (3) synthetic verification harness to validate recoveries and rollback behavior.
Out of scope: upstream model architecture changes, deep kernel optimizations, and changes to billing models.
Stakeholders: Runtime, Autoscale, Console, Observability, Solutions Engineering, SRE, Legal (for tenant contract language).
proposed_changes:
1) Add a control-plane API for defining 'degradation contracts' per tenant: budget window, allowed feature set reductions, fallback model variants, and automatic vs manual enforcement.
2) Implement a 'traffic shepherd' subsystem in the router/orchestrator that can: (a) detect SLO gate violations, (b) shift a configurable fraction of traffic to warmed standby pools or lower-cost model variants, (c) rate-limit high-variance tenants, and (d) surface decisions to Console and audit logs.
3) Build a synthetic verification harness (playback + injected load) that runs during canary and automated remediation to verify correctness of fallbacks and absence of regressions.
4) Expose tenant degradation state in Console with runbook-guided buttons: 'Enact Contract', 'Pause', 'Rollback', and 'Acknowledge'.
5) Telemetry: add new metrics and traces for 'degradation_decision', 'traffic_shepherd_actions', 'synthetic_verification_pass', and tenant-level SLO burn rate.
6) Runbooks: author operator playbooks mapping detection signals to stepwise mitigation and rollback criteria.
7) Billing/contract: product to draft tenant-visible language about temporary degraded-mode behavior and opt-in thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Control-plane API allows creation, update, and deletion of a degradation contract; contract fields validated and visible in Console.

A2: Router can automatically shift up to configured percent of a tenant's traffic to a warmed standby pool within target_time_ms <= 250ms after trigger condition, while preserving request ordering where necessary.
A3: Synthetic verification harness runs as part of canary and remediation; must detect failed fallback in >=90% of injected-failure scenarios and block rollout when verification fails.
A4: Console shows real-time tenant SLO burn, active degradation contract, and last synthetic verification result; operators can enact/rollback with audit trail.

A5: End-to-end integration tests: simulate tenant burst that would exceed degradation budget and validate that traffic shepherding reduces 99.9th percentile latency by >=30% compared to baseline within the remediation window.
A6: Runbook documented with explicit rollback gates tied to telemetry thresholds; on-call SRE can follow playbook to restore normal routing within SLA of 15 minutes.
A7: Security review completed (if required) and telemetry complies with PII constraints in Private deployments.
